hyperedges.label: Verifiable Deterministic Pairing (seed, signature, draw number, pure engine, exact math)
pg-boss Job Pipeline (offers, mail, push, season recalc, Glicko)
Phase Chaining Contract (phase, gate, inheritance, no-rematch scope, linearization)
Row to DTO layering per entity
Shared schema validation on both sides

nodes.label: Frontend/Backend Ownership Split (Marco / Lord Bel)
nodes.rationale: Two people each own one half; stay on your side and describe cross-boundary changes instead of making them.

nodes.label: shared/ as API Contract Boundary
nodes.rationale: A change in shared/ changes the other person's contract, so it must be flagged and consumers on the other side are not fixed unilaterally.

nodes.label: ponytail: Integration Seam Marker
nodes.rationale: Marks deliberate frontend-backend seams (data fetching, auth, validation) naming the backend contract a page waits for; removed only when the backend is wired.

nodes.label: Italian UI Text and Comments Convention
nodes.norm_label: italian ui text and comments convention

nodes.label: Node 26 Pin for Native Temporal
nodes.rationale: Node major 26 pinned in .nvmrc because it ships Temporal unflagged.

nodes.label: No Mailer Yet
nodes.rationale: Email verification, password reset and invitations all wait on a mailer.

nodes.label: PGlite In-Process Dev Database
nodes.rationale: Postgres compiled to WASM runs in-process with data in .data/pglite, so no local DB install is needed; same postgresql dialect and migrations as production.

nodes.label: db:generate / db:migrate / db:seed / db:studio
nodes.rationale: Run as standalone Node processes outside Nuxt, reading config via server/database/env.ts rather than runtimeConfig.

nodes.label: Dev Mock System (defineMock, server/mocks)
nodes.rationale: Lets a page be built before its endpoint exists or reproduce states the DB lacks; mocks run in a middleware before routing, win over real handlers, are dev-only via import.meta.dev, and are disabled rather than deleted.

nodes.label: Nuxt UI v4 + Tailwind 4 Frontend Stack
nodes.norm_label: nuxt ui v4 + tailwind 4 frontend stack

nodes.label: Node v24.11.0 Requirement (README)
nodes.rationale: README still states Node 24 and no test setup, outdated against CLAUDE.md (Node 26, test:backend).

nodes.label: Users API (/api/users, /api/users/:id, /api/users/me)
nodes.rationale: All user routes require a session; list and detail intentionally restricted to id and name, private fields only on /me.

nodes.label: UserSummary DTO
nodes.rationale: UserSummary is not a Player; sporting identity not implemented yet.

nodes.label: app/pages/hello.vue Contract Mismatch
nodes.rationale: hello.vue still reads email, createdAt, isActive from the list; frontend not modified by backend, must use minimal view or /me.

nodes.label: server/services/users.ts (getOwnAccount)
nodes.rationale: Reads with explicit Database dependency and no HTTP dependencies; future services coordinate authorization and transactions.

nodes.label: Pure Allowlist Mappers
nodes.rationale: Pure functions with allowlist and minimal sources: no queries, hashing, permission checks or writes; a mapper does not authorize a read.

nodes.label: Shared Schemas Validate and Normalize Contract
nodes.rationale: Persistent constraints stay in the DB; state- and authorization-dependent rules belong to use cases, not shared schemas.
nodes.norm_label: shared schemas validate and normalize contract

nodes.label: Offset Pagination with Informative Total
nodes.rationale: Total and page queries don't share a snapshot; future lists may use cursors without a universal exact count.

nodes.label: npm run test:backend (node --test)
nodes.rationale: No DB and no Nuxt; not end-to-end. Concurrent commands will need integration tests on real PostgreSQL since PGlite cannot substitute.

nodes.label: Current Results as Source of Truth (standings as read model)
nodes.rationale: Every standing is recomputable from results; no score is an updated field. Not event sourcing: current state plus history.
nodes.norm_label: current results as source of truth (standings as read model)

nodes.label: Versioned Config Frozen at Use (copy, not reference)
nodes.rationale: Tournament keeps a resolved copy of ruleset and policy; configuration is frozen, code is not, so a fixed tiebreak bug changes past standings if recalculated.
nodes.norm_label: versioned config frozen at use (copy, not reference)

nodes.label: Pure TypeScript Tournament Engine
nodes.rationale: Pairing and standings know neither Nuxt nor the DB; takes participants, results, config; testable with fixtures. Versioned package, verifiable from CLI like the FIDE pairing checker.

nodes.label: Seeded Randomness, Outcomes Saved as Facts
nodes.rationale: Seed generated by the server, chosen by no one; seed and engine version serve to verify, not re-run. Same input gives same output, so 'regenerate' is useless by construction.
nodes.norm_label: seeded randomness, outcomes saved as facts

nodes.label: Adding a Game = Writing a Composition
nodes.rationale: No DSL, no interpreter; a rule missing from the catalog is a new module, i.e. code.
nodes.norm_label: adding a game = writing a composition

nodes.label: DB Row Is Not the API Contract (row -> mapper -> DTO)
nodes.norm_label: db row is not the api contract (row -> mapper -> dto)

nodes.label: pg-boss for All Jobs (enqueued in same transaction)
nodes.rationale: Persistent cron runs once across instances; fromDrizzle(tx, sql) ties jobs to the change; Nitro tasks are experimental and per-instance.
nodes.norm_label: pg-boss for all jobs (enqueued in same transaction)

nodes.label: SSE Live with LISTEN/NOTIFY Fan-out
nodes.rationale: 30s keepalive under CapRover nginx 60s timeout, X-Accel-Buffering: no, ID-only payloads; a lost notification is fine since reconnecting clients reread the DB.

nodes.label: CapRover Deploy (always-on Node container)
nodes.rationale: Start with one instance, design for many; app container stateless, Postgres a separate CapRover app.

nodes.label: PWA Web Push (VAPID)
nodes.rationale: On iPhone push only works with the app installed to Home Screen, so nothing that must arrive goes only via push.

nodes.label: Email via SMTP (only from a job)
nodes.rationale: No irreplaceable provider: SMTP is a standard, provider in NUXT_MAIL_*; domain needs SPF, DKIM, DMARC.
nodes.norm_label: email via smtp (only from a job)

nodes.label: Player Identity Rules (on-the-fly, unclaimed, claim token)
nodes.rationale: No profile merge ever; the only defense is search-with-fuzzy-match before create. Claiming is not a merge.
nodes.norm_label: player identity rules (on-the-fly, unclaimed, claim token)

nodes.label: Removal = Anonymization
nodes.rationale: Results are tournament facts and stay; Player becomes 'removed player' so closed standings don't change.

nodes.label: Accepted Privacy Risks (minors, ownership)
nodes.rationale: Invite-only platform without privacy consultant; under-14 accounts and public minor profiles accepted, to revisit before public opening. Mitigations: noindex on minor profiles, warning on creation.

nodes.label: Two-Level Ruleset (Module Catalog + Composition)
nodes.rationale: Catalog is engine code changed by deploy; composition is a choice of modules and params by platform or organizer. Valibot schema generated from catalog drives validation and the creation form.

nodes.label: Catalog Categories (result shape, points, tiebreak, list, operational)
nodes.norm_label: catalog categories (result shape, points, tiebreak, list, operational)

nodes.label: Phase Architecture (ordered list in, ordered list out)
nodes.rationale: Input order is seeding, output order is standings; enables chaining. Each phase must linearize; final standings compose backward; operational settings are per phase.
nodes.norm_label: phase architecture (ordered list in, ordered list out)

nodes.label: No-Rematch Scope = Chain of Phases Inheriting Opponent History
nodes.norm_label: no-rematch scope = chain of phases inheriting opponent history

nodes.label: Round Limit Warning (rounds > players/2)
nodes.rationale: System warns, never prevents; recalculated at every drop since drops lower the limit.

nodes.label: Tournament Lifecycle (draft -> published -> registration_open -> checkin_open -> running -> finished / cancelled)
nodes.rationale: Pause is a round-clock property, not a tournament state.
nodes.norm_label: tournament lifecycle (draft -> published -> registration_open -> checkin_open -> running -> finished / cancelled)

nodes.label: Per-Tournament IANA Timezone and Temporal Date Math
nodes.rationale: Recurrences in local time, calendar offsets not durations, day deadlines end-of-day in tournament TZ, 'compatible' disambiguation for DST; native Temporal on Node 26, polyfill in frontend.
nodes.norm_label: per-tournament iana timezone and temporal date math

nodes.label: Three Orthogonal Registration Axes (seat, attendance, play)
nodes.rationale: Compressing them makes 'how many still in play at round 3' unanswerable; participant count needs three views.
nodes.norm_label: three orthogonal registration axes (seat, attendance, play)

nodes.label: Waitlist Promotion by Expiring Offer
nodes.rationale: Offer valid until 'tomorrow same time' in tournament TZ or check-in opening; seat reserved during the offer.

nodes.label: Check-in Opening as Single Freeze Point
nodes.rationale: One moment ends cancellations and automatic offers; no-check-in at start is a no_show drop kept in history.
nodes.norm_label: check-in opening as single freeze point

nodes.label: Weighted Blossom Maximum Matching Pairing
nodes.rationale: All rules become edge weights; always produces a complete pairing; avoids greedy dead-ends since there is no regenerate button.

nodes.label: Lexicographic Pairing Priorities (cardinality > no 2nd bye > no rematch > quadratic score diff > side > cosmetic)
nodes.rationale: Each level outweighs the max sum of all lower levels; integer weights in BigInt or under 2^53. Second bye judged worse than a rematch.
nodes.norm_label: lexicographic pairing priorities (cardinality > no 2nd bye > no rematch > quadratic score diff > side > cosmetic)

nodes.label: Manual Pairing Override with Mandatory Reason
nodes.rationale: Warns but never prevents; organizer is the authority in the room. Kept despite EventLink removing manual pairings for fraud; reason in history deemed sufficient.
nodes.norm_label: manual pairing override with mandatory reason

nodes.label: Two Bye Origins (structural, premium)
nodes.rationale: Bye is always a full win; opponent dropping after pairing is not a bye.

nodes.label: Round Lifecycle (generate -> publish -> start; draft|published|started|closed|cancelled)
nodes.rationale: Cancelling marks pairings and results as cancelled and discards the snapshot; nothing is deleted. Cheap only because standings are a read model.

nodes.label: Result Entry and Dispute Handling
nodes.rationale: One result row per match; first entry valid, contradictory second entry goes to history as rejected attempt and sets disputed. No-show is a loss followed by a drop.

nodes.label: Tournament History (app-written, same transaction, INSERT/SELECT only)
nodes.rationale: Trigger can't see app user or reason; single table per tournament; records also intentions that don't change state.
nodes.norm_label: tournament history (app-written, same transaction, insert/select only)

nodes.label: Clock as DB Fact ({ endsAt, pausedMs, status } + server now)
nodes.rationale: No server setInterval; client computes offset once and counts locally, no drift; SSE sends only state changes. Same logic as RoundTimer.
nodes.norm_label: clock as db fact ({ endsat, pausedms, status } + server now)

nodes.label: Two-Level Roles (org owner/admin; tournament head_judge/judge/scorekeeper)
nodes.rationale: No tournament 'organizer' role; Better Auth lacks per-resource permissions so tournament roles are our own table. Playing judge is an off-by-default tournament option, a match-level permission check.

nodes.label: Online Only with Paper Fallback
nodes.rationale: Offline writes would contradict server seed, single outcome per round, same-transaction history and first-result rule; offline and manual pairings were 90% of WER maintenance.

nodes.label: Notification Matrix (push + in app, email for seat offers)
nodes.norm_label: notification matrix (push + in app, email for seat offers)

nodes.label: Data Model Phase -> Round -> Match -> Board/Game
nodes.rationale: Slot model kept even though v1 matches are always two entities, so FFA can arrive without rewriting matches, results and standings.
nodes.norm_label: data model phase -> round -> match -> board/game

nodes.label: Tiebreak Catalog (OMW%, GW%, OGW%, VP, Buchholz, head-to-head, wins)
nodes.rationale: Floor and cap are function parameters (33% MTG, 25-75% Pokemon).
nodes.norm_label: tiebreak catalog (omw%, gw%, ogw%, vp, buchholz, head-to-head, wins)

nodes.label: Bye in Tiebreaks as Two Independent Parameters
nodes.rationale: Each preset reproduces its game's official rules; free-tournament default exclude/excluded. Forfeit wins count as real opponents, deliberately diverging from FIDE.
nodes.norm_label: bye in tiebreaks as two independent parameters

nodes.label: Standings Math Uses Only + - * /, min, max
nodes.rationale: Math.pow and similar change across Node versions; values rounded to declared precision before comparison.
nodes.norm_label: standings math uses only + - * /, min, max

nodes.label: Season Recalculation Job with Credit Realignment
nodes.rationale: Corrections apply in place even after season close and can change best-N of absent players; revocations and issuances in the same transaction; spent credits stay spent.
nodes.norm_label: season recalculation job with credit realignment

nodes.label: Best-N Season Ranking with Size Quotas
nodes.rationale: Uses placement, not path; size multiplier is the only correction. Ranking is a selection, not a sum.
nodes.norm_label: best-n season ranking with size quotas

nodes.label: Glicko Rating (separate from circuit points)
nodes.rationale: Only number not a pure function of results: RD decays with inactivity, needs periodic job or lazy calc.

nodes.label: Three-State Capacity (occupied / offer-reserved / free) DB Constraint
nodes.rationale: Bug source number one; registered < cap is wrong by construction; PGlite single connection won't surface races in dev.
nodes.norm_label: three-state capacity (occupied / offer-reserved / free) db constraint

nodes.label: Scanner-Safe One-Time Links (GET confirm, POST consume)
nodes.rationale: Mail scanners like Microsoft Safe Links open links before the recipient; scanners don't submit forms.
nodes.norm_label: scanner-safe one-time links (get confirm, post consume)

nodes.label: v1 Scope: First Real Tournament 29 Nov 2026 (free, swiss + top cut, individual)
nodes.rationale: Invite-only first release; accounts created by hand, results entered by staff only, no print or offline.
nodes.norm_label: v1 scope: first real tournament 29 nov 2026 (free, swiss + top cut, individual)

nodes.label: Milestones M0 Walking Skeleton -> M1 Swiss -> M2 Top Cut -> M3 Dress Rehearsal
nodes.norm_label: milestones m0 walking skeleton -> m1 swiss -> m2 top cut -> m3 dress rehearsal

nodes.label: Identifier Naming Conventions (English ids, PascalCase types, camelCase props, snake_case tables/enums)
nodes.rationale: One concept, one word: 'torneo' never 'evento', 'fase' never 'stage'.
nodes.norm_label: identifier naming conventions (english ids, pascalcase types, camelcase props, snake_case tables/enums)

nodes.label: Participant
nodes.rationale: The only thing pairing, results and standings know; name already used by the frontend; NOT start.gg's meaning.

nodes.label: drawNumber
nodes.rationale: One random number per participant instead of a draw per tie, because the tied group changes with every correction.

nodes.label: StandingsSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Per-round cache computed at close; for a finished tournament it is the shown standings; a deploy recalculates nothing by itself.

nodes.label: Penalty (warning, game loss, match loss, disqualification)
nodes.norm_label: penalty (warning, game loss, match loss, disqualification)

nodes.label: ByeCredit
nodes.rationale: One row per bye so partial spending and cross-tournament summing are row counts.

nodes.label: Topic 1: The Log - State + History, No Event Sourcing
nodes.rationale: Deleting facts and an append-only audit conflicted; chose family B (current state + app-written history). Audit alone doesn't justify event sourcing (Dudycz).
nodes.norm_label: topic 1: the log - state + history, no event sourcing

nodes.label: Event Sourcing (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Complex, costly to migrate in/out, poor to query, event schema versioned forever; Young and Dahan advise it only within a bounded context.

nodes.label: Topic 2: Reproducibility - Verify, Don't Re-run
nodes.rationale: Pairings and draws are saved facts; only standings are recomputed. Signature verifies a pairing with its version; recalculation uses today's code.

nodes.label: Math Keeps Changing (MacWright, Math.pow across Node)
nodes.norm_label: math keeps changing (macwright, math.pow across node)

nodes.label: FIDE Swiss Rules (C.04.2, C.04.3 Dutch, C.07 Tiebreaks)
nodes.norm_label: fide swiss rules (c.04.2, c.04.3 dutch, c.07 tiebreaks)

nodes.label: Fuhrlich, Cseh, Lenzner: Swiss as Max-Weight Matching
nodes.norm_label: fuhrlich, cseh, lenzner: swiss as max-weight matching

nodes.label: Topic 3: Config vs Code Boundary
nodes.rationale: Deck validators need external card data and legality, i.e. code; wargames don't fit the three result archetypes. Platform rulesets become repo files; event keeps resolved copy.

nodes.label: Topic 4: Bye in Tiebreaks
nodes.rationale: A fixed 100% virtual opponent contradicted parametric tiebreak modules and was used by no source; split into two parameters; ByeCredit separated from Qualification.

nodes.label: Play! Pokemon Rules (RK9 tiebreakers, Age Combined)
nodes.norm_label: play! pokemon rules (rk9 tiebreakers, age combined)

nodes.label: Topic 5: No-Rematch When No Complete Pairing Exists
nodes.rationale: Rematch as missing edge would silently prefer second byes; now all weights, second bye worse than rematch, declared choice.
nodes.norm_label: topic 5: no-rematch when no complete pairing exists

nodes.label: Dirac Theorem Round Limit (rounds <= n/2)
nodes.rationale: Up to half the players as rounds, a rematch-free complete pairing always exists; drops lower the limit.

nodes.label: Topic 6: Phase Continuity (day 2, multi-format)
nodes.rationale: Magic and Pokemon day 2 continue the same swiss; continuity has three independent components; no-rematch scope independent of phase.

nodes.label: Topic 7: Tournament Ownership and Roles
nodes.rationale: All platforms bind events to a container outliving people; Melee's two-level staff matches the need for external judges.

nodes.label: Tournament Platforms (EventLink, Melee.gg, start.gg, Challonge, TopDeck.gg, Limitless)
nodes.norm_label: tournament platforms (eventlink, melee.gg, start.gg, challonge, topdeck.gg, limitless)

nodes.label: Topic 8: Infrastructure Dependencies
nodes.rationale: 'No external service' reread as 'no irreplaceable provider'; pg-boss only; CapRover without pooler so LISTEN works.

nodes.label: Nitro Scheduled Tasks (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Experimental, not persistent, run once per instance.

nodes.label: Topic 9: Minors and Unclaimed Profiles
nodes.rationale: Not legal advice; GDPR art. 8, Italian art. 2-quinquies (14 years), EDPB 1/2024, Garante 2026 on aggregating minors' results.

nodes.label: GDPR / Codice privacy art. 2-quinquies / EDPB Guidelines
nodes.norm_label: gdpr / codice privacy art. 2-quinquies / edpb guidelines

nodes.label: Topic 10: Room Without Network
nodes.rationale: Hard part is reconciliation, not local execution; Background Sync absent on iOS.

nodes.label: WER -> EventLink Precedent (offline + manual pairing = 90% maintenance)
nodes.norm_label: wer -> eventlink precedent (offline + manual pairing = 90% maintenance)

nodes.label: Topic 11: Recurring Dates, Timezones, DST
nodes.rationale: EU DST abolition stalled; iCalendar TZID recurrences keep local time; timestamptz loses the zone so IANA name stored separately; move to Node 26.

nodes.label: Topic 12: Glossary and Naming Language
nodes.rationale: Mixed Italian/English identifiers and evento/torneo synonyms; adopted English ids, Tournament, Phase, Participant replaces Entrant.

nodes.label: Topic 13: v1 Scope and Milestones
nodes.rationale: Everything that could wait, waits; circuit-derived features only make sense after concluded tournaments exist; mailer deferred, overriding topic 8 decision 1.

nodes.label: Topic 14: Alignment with Frontend Model
nodes.rationale: Frontend was written on a provisional model marked ponytail:; added tournament lifecycle and 'results publication' term to disambiguate three meanings of publish.

nodes.label: shared/types/tournament.ts (provisional frontend model)
nodes.rationale: Flat Tournament, home/away Match, Standing without tiebreaks, TournamentConfig via Omit, startDate as Date; to be rewritten by the backend owner as endpoints arrive.

nodes.label: Frontend Pages to Adapt for v1 (/tournaments, /new, /[id], /settings, /display, /hello)
nodes.norm_label: frontend pages to adapt for v1 (/tournaments, /new, /[id], /settings, /display, /hello)

nodes.label: Dev-only Mock System
nodes.rationale: Fake data served by Nitro only in development: to work on a page before its endpoint exists and to reproduce on demand states the database lacks (empty list, 500, slow response).

nodes.label: defineMock()
nodes.rationale: Identity function existing only for contract checking and autocompletion inside the object literal.

nodes.label: server/mocks/index.ts (mock registry)
nodes.rationale: Registry stays explicit: import.meta.glob is a Vite feature unavailable in Nitro/rollup, and the list is the single place showing which mocks exist; a forgotten file never answers by mistake.

nodes.label: server/mocks/*.mock.ts
nodes.rationale: Data generated at module level with a fixed faker seed so ids survive restarts and detail lookups match list results.

nodes.label: MOCK_DATA: true header
nodes.rationale: Marks every fake response (set before calling data, so thrown errors carry it too) so real vs mocked calls are visible in the Network tab; absence on real handlers detects matching regressions.

nodes.label: Enabled mock wins over real handler
nodes.rationale: Mocks answer before routing so toggling a boolean compares mock and implementation; they also bypass authentication, which is why they work for endpoints that do not exist yet.
nodes.norm_label: enabled mock wins over real handler

nodes.label: Mock lifecycle (mock is never deleted)
nodes.rationale: After the handler lands the mock stays disabled in the registry to reproduce edge states on demand; being typed on shared/ types it stops compiling when the contract changes, which forces maintenance.

nodes.label: Dynamic import behind import.meta.dev
nodes.rationale: Nitro replaces import.meta.dev with false in builds so rollup drops mocks and faker (a devDependency); a static import would break npm ci --omit=dev && npm run build.

nodes.label: No mocks in production
nodes.rationale: An environment needing fake data uses a database seed, not this mechanism; verified by grep -r faker .output/server after build.

nodes.label: API Contract (shared/)
nodes.rationale: shared/ holds what crosses the wire; both sides import it, so a change there changes the other person's contract.

nodes.label: shared/schemas/ (Valibot input schemas)
nodes.rationale: Hand-written and contract-first (business rules, not table constraints); the same schema validates UForm and the handler body so they cannot drift; never generated via drizzle-valibot to keep Drizzle out of the client bundle; Italian messages written by hand.

nodes.label: DTO as field allowlist (row is not the contract)
nodes.rationale: DTO fields are written one by one so a new column never reaches the frontend by itself; never derive a DTO from a table type (Omit<UserRow,...>).
nodes.norm_label: dto as field allowlist (row is not the contract)

nodes.label: DTO variants compose, nest downward only
nodes.rationale: Smallest shape is the base and fuller ones extend it; summaries never hold their parent to avoid JSON cycles; variants created only when a real consumer needs one.
nodes.norm_label: dto variants compose, nest downward only

nodes.label: Dates as ISO strings on the wire
nodes.rationale: Nitro's Serialize maps Date to string in useFetch inference, so DTOs declare string to keep declared and inferred types identical; frontend converts back.
nodes.norm_label: dates as iso strings on the wire

nodes.label: Branded ids (shared/types/ids.ts)
nodes.rationale: Type-only brand (plain string in JSON) so passing a UserId where a TournamentId is expected fails to compile.

nodes.label: Two error shapes (ours vs Better Auth)
nodes.rationale: Our errors: createError with English statusMessage (h3 strips non-ASCII) and Italian text in message; Better Auth returns {code,message} read by its own client. Do not harmonise them.
nodes.norm_label: two error shapes (ours vs better auth)

nodes.label: Engine is pure TypeScript with own I/O types
nodes.rationale: No Nuxt/h3/Nitro/Drizzle/app imports and no DTOs or rows, so it stays extractable as a versioned package and decoupled from the API contract; services translate rows to engine input and back.
nodes.norm_label: engine is pure typescript with own i/o types

nodes.label: Deterministic engine with server-provided seed
nodes.rationale: Same input + seed gives same output; stable ordering, lowest index wins ties; no Math.random/Date.now; seed generated by the server with a cryptographic RNG when the round is created.

nodes.label: Exact integer/BigInt weights
nodes.rationale: No floating point in comparisons deciding pairings or rankings; lexicographic priority weights in BigInt or below 2^53.

nodes.label: Weighted maximum matching (blossom) pairing
nodes.rationale: Pairing never fails: no hard constraints, only weights in a fixed priority order, so a complete pairing is always returned.

nodes.label: Tiebreak catalogue modules (OMW%, GW%, Buchholz)
nodes.rationale: Core knows no tiebreak; ruleset picks an ordered list of modules with parameters; adding a game is composition, no DSL or interpreter.

nodes.label: Round generation signature {engineVersion, seed, input}
nodes.rationale: Verifying a round means engine(input, seed) == saved pairing; any output change for a given input is a new engine version.

nodes.label: Backend layering (schema, DTO, mapper, service, handler)
nodes.rationale: Output is mapped (trusted), input is validated then mapped (untrusted); handlers never touch a Row.
nodes.norm_label: backend layering (schema, dto, mapper, service, handler)

nodes.label: server/mappers/<entity>.ts
nodes.rationale: Only place rows and DTOs meet; pure functions with no queries, hashing, permission checks or writes; take minimal Pick<> sources.

nodes.label: server/services/<entity>.ts
nodes.rationale: Explicit Database parameter, no HTTP deps; actorId always comes from the session.

nodes.label: Spread a DTO, never a Row
nodes.rationale: TypeScript does not excess-property-check a spread, so spreading a row leaks every column.
nodes.norm_label: spread a dto, never a row

nodes.label: Input mapper toNewEntityRow()
nodes.rationale: Its return type (object literal typed NewRow) catches contract fields with no matching column that Drizzle would silently drop; also hosts non-1:1 mappings like password->passwordHash and session-derived organizerId.

nodes.label: server/utils/validation.ts (readInput, readQuery, readParams)
nodes.rationale: Single place where Valibot issues become a 400 with ApiErrorData; replaces h3 getValidated* helpers that nest payload at data.data.

nodes.label: Better Auth (self-hosted)
nodes.rationale: Email + password only; no 2FA, organizations, OAuth or mailer, so email verification and password reset are off.

nodes.label: /api/auth/** perimeter
nodes.rationale: Better Auth endpoints validate their own input and return their own {code,message} shape; they bypass readInput, ApiErrorData and mappers.

nodes.label: server/utils/auth.ts (requireSession, requireUserId, useAuth)
nodes.rationale: Only meeting point of auth and domain; useAuth is a lazy async singleton whose failed creation is not cached so the server can recover.

nodes.label: server/database/schema/auth.ts (sessions, accounts, verifications)
nodes.rationale: Written by hand so migrations come from db:generate; TS property names are the contract with Better Auth; password lives in accounts.password (scrypt).

nodes.label: Banning via session.create.before hook
nodes.rationale: Every login creates a session, so one hook covers all methods; banning does not close open sessions (call revokeUserSessions); isActive is an older separate flag to collapse if equivalent.

nodes.label: session.cookieCache disabled
nodes.rationale: With it on the server trusts the cookie over the database, letting a banned user browse until the cache expires.

nodes.label: Postgres everywhere (PGlite local, postgres-js prod)
nodes.rationale: One schema and one set of migrations; PGlite runs Postgres in WASM in-process so dev needs nothing installed; production Postgres is operated outside the repo via NUXT_DATABASE_URL. PGlite has no pool, so concurrency bugs need a real Postgres.

nodes.label: server/database/schema/index.ts
nodes.rationale: Forgetting the export * line fails silently: no migration and no error.

nodes.label: PGlite variable import specifier
nodes.rationale: Bundler cannot resolve it statically, keeping 17 MB of WASM out of .output and PGlite a devDependency; a normal import would quadruple the production build.

nodes.label: Branded id column uuid('id').$type<UserId>()
nodes.rationale: Rows arrive branded so mappers need no cast; branded types disable shorthand equality filters, so use where: { id: { eq: id } }.

nodes.label: orderBy tiebreaker for lists
nodes.rationale: defaultNow() is the transaction timestamp, so rows from one statement share it and equal sort keys make page boundaries non-deterministic.

nodes.label: Frontend app/ (Nuxt UI v4, Tailwind 4)
nodes.rationale: Components take DTOs as props and pages own state; UI-only types in app/types/, API response types in shared/types/ because server code cannot import from app/.

nodes.label: Do not annotate useFetch generic
nodes.rationale: The annotation overrides Nitro inference and hides mismatches with the handler; only mock-only endpoints use the generic, removed when the handler lands.

nodes.label: FetchError<ApiErrorData> handling
nodes.rationale: Show error.data.message, put error.data.fields back into the form, never read error.statusMessage.

nodes.label: app/middleware/auth.global.ts (authWhitelist)
nodes.rationale: Uses authClient.useSession(useFetch) so the session is read server-side with request cookies and reused on hydration.

nodes.label: projector layout (forced dark, text-screen scale)
nodes.rationale: Dark forced via .dark class on its own root so projection stays dark while the app runs light; used by /tournaments/[id]/display.

nodes.label: app/config/navigation.ts (appHeader, sideMenu, sideMenuFooter)
nodes.rationale: Navigation items are data, not markup in layouts/default.vue.

nodes.label: TournamentForm component
nodes.rationale: Shared by /tournaments/new and /tournaments/[id]/settings via defineModel + submit emit so form fields change in one place.

nodes.label: RoundTimer component
nodes.rationale: Starts its clock in onMounted with now=null until then to avoid SSR hydration mismatch; pattern to preserve in time-dependent components.

nodes.label: Mocks rule (frontend-owned server files)
nodes.rationale: A mock describes the contract the backend is expected to implement; response types in shared/types/ make it a shared/ change to report to the backend.

nodes.label: Theming in three layers
nodes.rationale: Primitives, per-theme values, semantic aliases; use semantic classes over hardcoded colors.

nodes.label: light.css / dark.css (--app-gradient)
nodes.rationale: :root and .dark have equal specificity so dark.css must remain the last import in main.css.
